question:
Consider the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. 
(a) Find a vector $\vec{c}$ perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.
(b) Show that $\vec{c}$ is unique up to scalar multiple.
(c) If $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\theta$ with $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$, find $\cos\theta$.
(d) Compute the projection of $\vec{a}$ onto $\vec{b}$ and interpret geometrically.
explanation:
(a) $\vec{c} = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$
$= \begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & 5\end{vmatrix}$
$= \hat{i}((-3)5 - 1\cdot4) - \hat{j}(2\cdot5 - 1(-1)) + \hat{k}(2\cdot4 - (-3)(-1))$
$= \hat{i}(-19) - \hat{j}(11) + \hat{k}(5)$
Thus $\vec{c} = -19\hat{i} - 11\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.

(b) The cross product of two nonparallel vectors is perpendicular to both and unique up to nonzero scalar multiples. Thus $\vec{c} = \lambda (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$.

(c) $\vec{a}+\vec{b} = (1,1,6)$
$\cos \theta = \frac{\vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a}+\vec{b})}{|\vec{c}|\,|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|}$
Dot product: $-19(1) -11(1) +5(6) = 0$
Thus $\cos\theta = 0$. Hence angle is $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

(d) Projection of $\vec{a}$ onto $\vec{b}$:
$\text{proj}_{\vec{b}} \vec{a} = \frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|^2}\vec{b}$
$\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = -9$
$|\vec{b}|^2 = 42$
$\text{proj}_{\vec{b}} \vec{a} = \frac{-9}{42}\vec{b}$
$= \frac{9}{42}\hat{i} - \frac{36}{42}\hat{j} - \frac{45}{42}\hat{k}$
Geometrically this represents the component of $\vec{a}$ along $\vec{b}$.

options.A:
(a) $\vec c=19\hat i+11\hat j-5\hat k$
(b) $\vec c$ is unique without scalar multiples
(c) $\cos\theta=1$
(d) $\operatorname{proj}_{\vec b}\vec a=\frac{9}{42}\vec b$
options.B:
(a) $\vec c=-19\hat i+11\hat j+5\hat k$
(b) Any vector is perpendicular to both $\vec a$ and $\vec b$
(c) $\cos\theta=-1$
(d) $\operatorname{proj}_{\vec b}\vec a=\frac{9}{42}\hat i-\frac{36}{42}\hat j+\frac{45}{42}\hat k$
options.C:
(a) $\vec c=-19\hat i-11\hat j+5\hat k$
(b) It is unique up to non-zero scalar multiple because any common perpendicular is parallel to $\vec a\times\vec b$
(c) $\cos\theta=0$
(d) $\operatorname{proj}_{\vec b}\vec a=\frac{-9}{42}\vec b=\frac{9}{42}\hat i-\frac{36}{42}\hat j-\frac{45}{42}\hat k$
options.D:
(a) $\vec c=2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k$
(b) It is unique only when $\vec a=\vec b$
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac12$
(d) $\operatorname{proj}_{\vec b}\vec a=\frac{-9}{14}\vec b$
